subject: Post-call: integration constraints, JSON reliability & retry patterns
messages:
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwoodinference.com>
To: Samir Rao <samir@quantforge.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwoodinference.com>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 1 Jun 2027 15:12:00 +0000
Subject: Post-call recap — integration constraints, JSON reliability & retry patterns

Samir / Priya — great to meet you both today. Quick written recap and proposed next steps so engineering can start scoping. I copied Neha (SE) and Sergio (AE owner).

Call summary (short)
- Use case: QuantForge wants an inference stack for human-in-the-loop document enrichment + reranking. Low-latency front door (~200–300ms P95) for live UI with bulk/async jobs for nightly enrichment.
- Key constraints you raised: strict JSON output required for downstream pipelines, enterprise auth (SSO + token rotation), and an auditable retry behavior for failed generations.

Integration/high-priority asks for scoping
1) SDK & auth: you asked about an SDK starting snippet and whether we support short-lived keys / mTLS. We support API keys + optional customer-managed mTLS in Private deployments; for Hosted we recommend short-lived tokens via our session API and KMS integration for rotation.
2) Routing / fallbacks: want a primary-realtime model with deterministic fallbacks when the low-latency tier is at capacity. We propose policy: route to low-latency variant (gpt-small-latency) with automatic fallback to gpt-eco with structured-output constraints enabled.
3) Structured output reliability: you emphasized a strict JSON schema and deterministic decoding. Recommended pattern: constrained-decoding + schema validation step, followed by a retry-with-relaxed-templating (soft-retry) and finally structured reparse/repair with a small deterministic fixer if still invalid.
4) Embeddings & rerank: indexing pipeline will use embeddings for recall, then a lightweight reranker for ordering; we should discuss index sharding and candidate set size.

Attachments: redwood-postcall-recap.pdf (this summary + MAP), example-constrained-schema.json (sample schema we recommend).

Proposed next steps
- Neha to propose a short technical note describing validation + retry semantics (by EOD Wednesday).
- QuantForge to share an example JSON spec for one canonical enrichment response (Priya).
- Schedule a 60–min technical workshop (engineers + SEs) to go over SDK init, auth flows, and a live demo of constrained decoding — suggested slots Thurs/Fri PST.

Can you confirm those next steps and share preferred time windows for the workshop?

Thanks,
Tessa Morgan
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Thanks Tessa — that matches our notes. Quick clarifications from our side:
- On schema: we'll send a canonical example (JSON) but want to understand how strict the runtime enforcement is. If a model produces slightly malformed JSON, do you reject, attempt repair, or run a secondary validation + call?
- Retry semantics: we want to avoid silent reordering of results; retries should be idempotent and observable (audit logs). How do you surface retries in logs/console?
- Auth: we need SSO for team access and short-lived keys for service-to-service. Is there an automated rotation integration with Okta/Azure AD?

We'll attach the canonical example and our security questionnaire later today. Preferred workshop windows: Thurs 10:00–12:00 PST or Fri 14:00–17:00 PST.

From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
To: Samir Rao <samir@quantforge.com>, Priya Shah <priya.shah@quantforge.com>
Cc: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwoodinference.com>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 2 Jun 2027 09:20:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Post-call recap — integration constraints, JSON reliability & retry patterns

Samir — quick technical note as promised, high level + practical patterns you can review before the workshop. Attaching an example schema (example-constrained-schema.json) and a snippet for SDK initialization in case you want to trial locally.

1) SDK + auth
- Hosted: API keys (rotate via Console) or short-lived tokens issued by our session endpoint. We have a hosted connector for Okta/OIDC that issues short-lived tokens; customers using SSO can map Okta groups to Console roles.
- Private: can be configured with mTLS and HSM-backed keys.
- Initialization snippet (pseudo):
  - import RedwoodClient from '@redwood/inference-sdk'
  - client = new RedwoodClient({endpoint: 'https://api.redwood.ai', apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_KEY, timeoutMs: 60000})
  - provide bearer token or mTLS cert when in Private mode

2) Structured output enforcement patterns
We recommend a three-tier policy implemented in the request pipeline:
  A) Constrained decoding: use constrained decoding / token list + anchoring prompts to steer model to produce valid JSON where possible. This reduces error rates significantly for small schemas.
  B) Schema validation: run a strict JSON Schema validator on the generated output. If invalid, perform a deterministic soft-retry (same prompt + stronger anchoring + explicit "return only valid JSON" instruction).
  C) Repair & fallback: if soft-retry fails after N attempts (N configurable, default 2), run a deterministic repair pass (parse errors -> predictable corrections) and flag the item for human review if repair changes > threshold.
Notes:
- We surface all retries in audit logs and the Console (token-level timeline + retry count). You get a per-request trace id that links generation attempts; this is retained for 90 days on Hosted and configurable for Private.
- For idempotency: we recommend adding a client-generated request id and using our idempotency token header to avoid duplicate downstream side-effects when retries are performed.

3) Validation + retry patterns (practical defaults)
- Max attempts for validation-retry: 2 automated attempts + 1 repair pass.
- Backoff between attempts: jittered fixed 200–400ms (keeps UI responsive).
- Circuit breaker rules at per-route level: open the circuit after 5 validation-failures / minute to avoid hammering the model during upstream incidents.

4) Embeddings & rerank guidance
- Indexing: store up-to-date embeddings (64–512 dimension depending on quantization) and keep candidate sets to ~100 for UI latency targets.
- Rerank: run a lightweight cross-encoder reranker that scores candidates; for expensive rerankers we recommend a cached top-N + asynchronous re-rank to improve final quality without hurting the UX.

5) Example observability hooks
- Request-level: trace id, attempts, schema-validation boolean, repair-flag, chosen-fallback-model
- Aggregates: validation-failure-rate per route, average retries per request, repair-success-rate

I'll bring a runnable demo of constrained decoding + validator to the workshop so we can test against your canonical spec.

--
Neha Kapoor
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
